submitter: bugfix_302_design_repair_verification lane, acting on bugs_open/317 (owner decision 3, 2026-08-19)
rationale:
ROUND 3. Round 2 was REVISE on a gating MISSING from editquality, and it was right in the way that matters most: my rationale asserted a change that was not in my own edit list. Round 2's other objections are answered below by measurement or code.

THE GATING MISSING — 'the rationale states the pre-image is now recorded in the lane, presented as a completed action, but no edit in the plan creates this file'. Correct. The file exists and was committed (845c0a362), but the plan did not list it, so the submission asserted a change its own diff did not show. THE EDIT IS NOW LISTED. ⚠ This is the SECOND time in two days a seat has caught this exact shape from me — yesterday I claimed a register entry was amended in the same commit when I had amended a different one. Both are logged in WRONG_CALLS.md, and the mechanical check I am now applying is: for every file the prose says changed, confirm an edit names it.

GUARDIAN'S MEDIUM was the strongest objection of the round and it exposed a genuine gap: the migration verified the TEXT of the rewritten pre_query, not its EXECUTABILITY — 'a single misplaced comma in the tail concatenation is invisible until the next scheduler tick', on a task that fires every 120s. Answered two ways, both empirical. (1) The rewritten predicate was read back from the live column and put through EXPLAIN: it parses and plans cleanly. Note EXPLAIN without ANALYZE plans WITHOUT executing, which matters here because the predicate contains an UPDATE inside a CTE — so this proves parseability without mutating anything. (2) Better than any static check: the task has been running on the rewritten predicate since 10:03Z. At the time of writing last_triggered_at and last_completed_at are equal and 83 seconds old, and agent_error_log carries ZERO errors mentioning this task, its predicate or pre_query since the change — roughly 22 clean executions. The objection is nonetheless correct as a matter of DISCIPLINE, and the ordering it implies (prove it runs, then let the scheduler find out) is what a future migration in this family should follow; that is now in the register entry.

REUSE_AGENT'S MEDIUM asked the right question and I had not shown the work: does the existing TestEveryItemTypeIsVerifiedOrAnAcknowledgedGap — whose name describes a 'verified OR acknowledged gap' contract — already cover this? It does not, and the demonstration is exact rather than arguable. That test's subject is VERIFIER COVERAGE: no type may hold both a verifier and a gap entry, every gap entry must carry a reason and a known category, nothing is silently unverified. Its registry, itemTypesWithoutVerifiers, is a list of types WITHOUT verifiers and why. **dark_section_audit is ALREADY IN that registry, as catMechanical with a written reason** — so that test was fully satisfied by exactly the state this lockstep was written to catch: a type with an acknowledged verifier gap, a gate-1b roster entry, and no sweep exclusion. The two tests answer different questions about different lists, and the existing one is green in the failure case. TestEveryCheckProducedItemTypeIsClassified likewise scans source for ItemType literals and speaks to classification, not to the sweep.

GUARDIAN'S LOWS about what the council cannot verify from its own schema (the live pre_query text, the exclusion count, the sibling-sweep claim) are accepted as stated limits rather than argued with. The queries are in grounded_in so a human can re-run them in seconds; scheduled_tasks is not in the reviewable schema and I cannot change that from here.

DEBUG_HISTORIAN'S LOW — the sketch elided the `n` computation behind '...'. Shown in full below: the count is SELECTed from the live table into `n` and compared, not asserted.

ARCHITECTURE'S watch item (a THIRD completion-gate class should become a registry rather than another pairwise test) is recorded in the register beside the two-gate note, and I agree it wants a stronger forcing function than a comment if it ever recurs.

plan.summary: Widen the claimed-item-timeout exclusion contract from 'has a registered verifier' to 'has a registered verifier OR a noChangeGates entry', apply it to the live scheduled_tasks.pre_query via a guarded migration, and move the parity guard to the one package that can read both rosters.

edits.rationale: Owning pipeline: the work-item dispatch/completion path (site-work-orchestrator and the dispatch loops), whose completions this sweep short-circuits. Adds dark_section_audit to the exclusion list on the LIVE column. Guarded as a DO block rather than a bare UPDATE: a read-before-write anchor aborts if the predicate has moved since this was written, an idempotence check aborts on a second application rather than appending a duplicate, and the post-write verification RAISEs — because ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result set, so a verification block built from SELECTs cannot stop the COMMIT. 220 is deliberately NOT edited: it is applied history and editing it would make its recorded checksum a lie.
Removes the added type and verifies the removal by RAISE. Its own comment states the cost of using it: applying the rollback re-opens bugs_open/317.
edits.sketch:
+UPDATE scheduled_tasks SET pre_query = replace(pre_query, ', dark_section_audit', '') ...
+IF n <> 0 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'ABORT: rollback did not remove it'; END IF;

edits.rationale: The widened guard, in the only package that can see both rosters. Asserts the contract in BOTH directions over the union, and asserts each roster is non-empty SEPARATELY so a failure names which one went missing — without that, emptying noChangeGates would silently narrow the guard back to the gate-2-only contract this change exists to widen. Reads the NEWEST matching migration, because 220 stays as history and a later migration owns the live predicate.

edits.rationale: FUNCTION-LEVEL modify, not a file removal — my round-1 label said 'remove' and two seats correctly objected. [MEASURED] the file retains TestEveryItemTypeIsVerifiedOrAnAcknowledgedGap, TestEveryCheckProducedItemTypeIsClassified and TestVerifierCoverageIsReported, none touched. The one lockstep function is deleted because once the exclusion list carries a type with no registered verifier its reverse direction fails BY DESIGN — proven to fail before deletion, not assumed. A comment is left in its place explaining where the guard went and the import-direction reason it could not stay, so no reader concludes a guard was silently dropped.

grounded_in: Migration 220's own comment, which states the contract being widened: 'The item_type exclusion is the LOCKSTEP TWIN of the RegisterVerifier() calls in platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks/: those item types have a Go verifier that…'

MEASURED 2026-08-19, the live predicate BEFORE: 13 item types, exactly matching the 13 RegisterVerifier/RegisterVerifierWithPolicy call sites — so the gate-2 lockstep was intact and the gap was specifically gate 1b.

MEASURED 2026-08-19, archive-inclusive (site_work_items UNION site_work_items_archive, because the live table is a ~7-day window): 0 of 30 dark_section_audit and 0 of 498 hardcoded_section_colors completions carry the sweep's completed_by_step shape. Never fired.

MEASURED 2026-08-19: scheduled_tasks 'claimed-item-timeout' enabled=true interval_seconds=120; 'improvement-sweep' enabled=false; 'site-discovery-rotation-design' enabled=false. The sweep runs constantly; it is the CLAIMING that is absent, which is why this is latent rather than structural.

VERIFIED at the live column after applying: the exclusion list holds 14 item types and its set is IDENTICAL to the one parsed out of the declared migration file; dark_section_audit appears exactly once; a second application ABORTS with 'this migration has been applied'.

Mutation matrix, exit-status gated with an unmutated control and both files restored byte-identical (diff -q): drop the type from the list -> RED ('has a noChangeGates entry (gate 1b) but is NOT excluded'); add a type no gate can grade -> RED ('NO gate can grade it'); empty noChangeGates -> RED ('gate 1b is inert').

The import direction that forced the package move: platform/orchestration/actions imports platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks (verified in complete_work_item_verification.go's import block), so a test in discovery_checks cannot read noChangeGates at any cost.

bugs_open/006 §C is why the reverse direction must stay: the sweep's generic branch exists because 15 of 18 types had no evidence test and were re-running finished work, so an over-wide exclusion list reintroduces that churn.

MEASURED 2026-08-19, answering guardian: SELECT name, enabled FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE pre_query ILIKE '%item_type NOT IN%' returns exactly ONE row, claimed-item-timeout itself. No sibling sweep shares the convention.

MEASURED 2026-08-19, answering editquality and guardian on the mislabel: verifier_coverage_test.go still contains 3 test functions after the edit (TestEveryItemTypeIsVerifiedOrAnAcknowledgedGap, TestEveryCheckProducedItemTypeIsClassified, TestVerifierCoverageIsReported). The edit is a function-level modify, not a file removal.

Mutation M10 (round 2), the gating objection made falsifiable: inserting a prose line containing the literal exclusion clause above the real declaration makes the guard FAIL with 'the exclusion clause in 482_... parsed to "...", which is not an item_type'. Restored byte-identical, control green. Run on a clean `git archive HEAD` overlay carrying only this file, because another session holds an uncommitted duplicate-symbol build break in the package (reWindowOnload).

The import edge the guardian asked to see confirmed rather than asserted: platform/orchestration/actions already imports platform/orchestration/actions/discovery_checks in PRODUCTION code (complete_work_item_verification.go's import block), so the test adds no new edge and the reverse edge cannot exist — which is the reason the guard had to move package at all.

MEASURED 2026-08-19 ~10:50Z, answering guardian's executability medium: the rewritten pre_query was read back from the live column and put through EXPLAIN — it parses and plans cleanly (plan head: 'Result ... CTE completed_by_orchestration -> Update on site_work_items wi'). EXPLAIN without ANALYZE plans without executing, which matters because the predicate contains an UPDATE.

MEASURED 2026-08-19 ~10:49Z, the empirical half of the same objection: claimed-item-timeout's last_triggered_at equals last_completed_at at 10:47:53Z (83s old, interval 120s), and agent_error_log holds ZERO rows since 10:03Z mentioning the task, 'item_type NOT IN' or 'pre_query'. ~22 clean executions on the rewritten predicate.

The prior-art demonstration reuse_agent asked for: itemTypesWithoutVerifiers ALREADY contains dark_section_audit (catMechanical, with a written reason), so TestEveryItemTypeIsVerifiedOrAnAcknowledgedGap was fully GREEN in exactly the state this lockstep exists to catch — a type with an acknowledged verifier gap, a gate-1b roster entry, and no sweep exclusion. The two tests pin different lists.
